function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick guide to help you find the perfect place to order a cake—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty shop, or a convenient online option: | Category | What to Look For | Why It Might Be Right for You | |----------|------------------|------------------------------| | **Local Bakeries** | • In‑person storefront or website
• Custom design options
• Fresh, made‑to‑order cakes | • Supports your community
• Often offers unique flavors & décor
• You can see samples or talk to the baker directly | | **Specialty Cake Shops** | • Known for elaborate designs (e.g., wedding cakes)
• Offer themed or seasonal collections | • Great for big events or when you want a show‑stopping centerpiece | | **Online Marketplaces** | • Etsy (handmade/custom cakes)
• Shopify sites of independent bakers | • Browse many sellers in one place
• Read reviews & see photos before ordering | | **Food Delivery Apps** | • Uber Eats, DoorDash, Postmates, Grubhub, SkipTheDishes (Canada), Deliveroo (UK), Swiggy (India) | • Fast delivery from local restaurants & bakeries
• Easy to compare prices & read ratings | | **Grocery Delivery Services** | • Instacart, Amazon Fresh, Shipt, Ocado (UK), BigBasket (India) | • Order a pre‑made cake from a supermarket
• Convenient if you’re already shopping for groceries | | **Specialty Food Stores** | • Whole Foods, Trader Joe’s, local health food co‑ops | • Good for vegan, gluten‑free, or organic cake options | | **Catering Companies** | • Local catering firms that offer dessert packages | • Ideal if you’re planning a party and want a full dessert spread | ### How to Choose 1. **Event Size & Type** * Small birthday → local bakery or grocery store cake. * Wedding or large celebration → specialty cake shop or custom baker. 2. **Dietary Needs** * Gluten‑free, vegan, keto → look for bakeries that specialize in those diets or check the product description on grocery delivery sites. 3. **Delivery Time & Reliability** * Check delivery windows on food apps; some allow you to schedule a specific time. * For custom cakes, confirm the baker’s lead time (often 1–2 weeks). 4. **Budget** * Pre‑made cakes from supermarkets are usually the cheapest. * Custom designs can range from $50 to several hundred dollars depending on size, complexity, and ingredients. 5. **Reviews & Photos** * On platforms like Yelp, Google Maps, or the bakery’s own site, look at recent customer photos and comments. * On Etsy, read seller ratings and open the “Open Shop” link to see their portfolio. ### Quick Starter List (by Region) | Region | Popular Platforms / Sites | |--------|---------------------------| | **United States** | • Local bakeries via Google Maps or Yelp
• Etsy (search “custom cake”)
• Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub | | **Canada** | • Local bakeries via Google Maps or Yelp Canada
• SkipTheDishes, DoorDash Canada
• Instacart Canada | | **United Kingdom** | • Local bakeries via Google Maps or Yell.com
• Deliveroo, Uber Eats UK
• Ocado | | **Australia** | • Local bakeries via Google Maps or Yellow Pages
• Uber Eats Australia, Menulog
• Woolworths Online | | **India** | • Local bakeries via Google Maps or Justdial
• Swiggy, Zomato, Foodpanda
• BigBasket, Grofers | ### Final Tips - **Ask About Ingredients** – If you have allergies or preferences, confirm the ingredients list before ordering. - **Confirm Delivery Address** – Some services require a delivery address that matches the billing address for security reasons. - **Tip the Baker** – If you’re ordering a custom cake, it’s customary to tip the baker (usually 10–15% of the total cost). Happy cake hunting! If you let me know your city or specific dietary needs, I can narrow down the best options for you.
